audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gives Tryndamere four of seven stages and Malphite none in a lane Malphite wins 57.17% over 1067 games — his best matchup in this slice. It also contradicts the entry's own text at every stage from 4-5 onward: whys[3] 'your trades flip', whys[5] 'his crit autos barely dent you', whys[6] 'keeps you favoured in any straight duel'.
audit.why: Levels 1-3 are genuinely his: Spinning Slash closes from 650 on 12s and Battle Fury turns early autos into crits before Thunderclap or Ground Slam exist. But from Level 4-5 Malphite has an attack-speed reduction against a champion whose entire damage output is basic attacks, and the chart should say so.
audit.corrected: Tryndamere owns Levels 1-3. From Levels 4-5 onward every stage is Malphite's, matching the 57.17% headline and the entry's own reasoning.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2], mid and whys[4] all resolve Level 6 the same way — 'wait out the 5s Undying Rage' — with no cooldowns on either ultimate and no mention of what he does with the time.
audit.why: Undying Rage is 120/100/80s and Unstoppable Force is 130/115/100s, so his ultimate is back before yours at every rank. And waiting it out is not passive: Bloodlust is a flat 12s heal that scales with the Fury he banks, and his attack damage rises as his health falls, so the five seconds you spend waiting are five seconds he spends at maximum AD healing himself back up. Without Grievous Wounds, out-lasting the immortality does not finish the job.
audit.corrected: Undying Rage 120/100/80s against your 130/115/100s — his is up first every rank. Out-lasting it only works with Grievous Wounds, because Bloodlust heals him back on a flat 12s and his AD is highest while he is lowest.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tryndamere.json (R cd 120/100/80; Q Bloodlust cd 12, heal, 'increasing his Attack Damage as he is more and more wounded')

audit.whatIsWrong: early says 'His W slows you and steals your move speed for the all-in, so respect that as your cue to back off'. Mocking Shout does not steal Move Speed, and the advice it produces is exactly backwards.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Tryndamere lets out an insulting cry, decreasing surrounding champions' Attack Damage. Enemies with their backs turned to Tryndamere also have their Move Speed reduced.' The slow is conditional on facing away from him. Backing off is what triggers it. The correct read is the opposite of what the entry says: when he shouts, keep facing him and walk backwards, or do not walk at all — and the attack-damage reduction half of the ability is worthless against Malphite, whose damage comes from Armor and AP.
audit.corrected: Mocking Shout (14s, 850 range) only slows enemies whose backs are turned — turning to run is what makes it work. Face him and back out, or do not run at all. Its AD reduction does nothing to you.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry never names one of his abilities — everything is 'his E gap-close', 'his spin', 'his W slow', 'Fury'. It also never states the single interaction that decides the matchup.
audit.why: Every point of Tryndamere's damage is a basic attack: Battle Fury converts Fury into critical strike chance, and there is no ability damage in the kit at all. Ground Slam reduces attack speed on a flat 7s from 400 range, and its own damage is calculated from Malphite's Armor. That is a hard counter to his entire damage profile and it is the reason armour is right here in a way it is not in most Malphite matchups. The entry gestures at it but never puts the two facts side by side.
audit.corrected: Battle Fury (P) turns Fury into crit chance and every point of his damage is a basic attack. Ground Slam cuts attack speed on a flat 7s and scales its damage off your Armor — one stat both defends you and powers the counter.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tryndamere.json (P Battle Fury; no ability damage scaling)

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Bait his E or his spin' — the entry names the same ability twice as if they were two things, and attaches no cooldown to it.
audit.why: Spinning Slash is the E and the spin; it is his only gap-closer and his only escape, on 12s at rank 1 falling to 8s, 650 range. The seconds after he spins are the entire commit window in this lane, and the number is what makes that actionable.
audit.corrected: Spinning Slash is his gap-closer and his escape both, 650 range on 12s at rank 1. Commit in the seconds after he spends it.

edits.before: Tryndamere owns the opening — at levels 1-2 you have no trade button, just Granite Shield and a Q poke, so he can stack Fury on the wave, E in and crit you down before Thunderclap or Ground Slam exist to answer. Don't contest last-hits inside his E range; farm with Seismic Shard from max distance and let your shield refresh between his pokes. His W slows you and steals your move speed for the all-in, so respect that as your cue to back off, not trade.
edits.after: Tryndamere owns the opening — at levels 1-2 you have Granite Shield and a Seismic Shard, nothing else, while Battle Fury banks Fury off the wave and turns his autos into crits. Spinning Slash closes 650 on a 12s cooldown, so do not contest last-hits inside it; farm at max range and let the shield refresh. One thing to unlearn: Mocking Shout only slows enemies whose backs are turned. Running is what makes it work. When he shouts, face him and walk out backwards; its AD cut does nothing to you.

edits.before: This is where the lane turns. Once Thunderclap is up you get bonus armor and AoE empowered autos, and Ground Slam's attack-speed slow directly cripples his crit-spin DPS — every point of armor you stack makes both abilities hit harder while his autos do less. Bait his E or his spin, then drop Ground Slam to slow his attack speed and trade back. At 6, Unstoppable Force flips it fully: he can E away or burn Undying Rage, but you can simply wait out the 5-second immortality and finish, or use R to lock him for a gank.
edits.after: This is where the lane turns. Every point of armour you buy defends those autos and grows Ground Slam at the same time. Commit in the seconds after Spinning Slash. At 6 you get Unstoppable Force, but out-lasting Undying Rage only works if you bought Grievous Wounds — Bloodlust is a flat 12s heal and his AD is highest when he is lowest.

notes: BIGGEST FIX: early told the player that Mocking Shout 'slows you and steals your move speed', and to treat it as the cue to back off. It does not steal Move Speed, and backing off is precisely what triggers it — Riot's text slows only 'enemies with their backs turned to Tryndamere'. The corrected play is to face him and walk out backwards. Its other half, the attack-damage reduction, does nothing to a Malphite whose damage comes from Armor and AP. SECOND: the entry named none of his abilities and never put the decisive fact on the page — Battle Fury pays out in critical strikes and Tryndamere has no ability damage at all, so Ground Slam's flat-7s attack-speed cut answers one hundred percent of his output, and armour both defends it and scales Ground Slam. This is the rare Malphite matchup where stacking armour is right for both reasons at once, and the entry never said why. THIRD: 'wait out the 5s Undying Rage' appeared three times with no cooldowns. Undying Rage is 120/100/80s against Unstoppable Force's 130/115/100s — his is back first at every rank — and Bloodlust is a flat 12s heal whose value rises as his health falls, so waiting it out without Grievous Wounds just hands him the heal. Anti-heal is flagged in _missing-interactions.json and appeared in the full layer only as the bare title 'Skip anti-heal'. UNVERIFIED: the '5-second' duration on Undying Rage is not in the kit file (Riot's text gives no duration). I left the existing wording rather than restate or remove the number.
